narration: Darkness, and then a floor of it: you feel cool, pale ground settle beneath your boots, fine as ash and faintly silver. Far to the north, a single small light flickers, amber and patient, as if it has been waiting for someone to look.

critique: The pale ash plain reads as a calm, silvery floor, and the soft glow around the Wanderer is a lovely touch. But the horizon is a hard dark band and the overview shows the disc ending in a visible curved edge against the void. The amber lantern, the story's one warm note, is invisible in the story view, so there's no pull northward. I'm steering toward a cold indigo-silver world with a faint horizon haze and one warm amber beacon.

Make the beacon readable at 40 m. Raise the core size to 0.3 and the halo opacity to 0.35, and add a larger soft sprite glow of about 2.5 m in #ffb347 at 0.15 opacity. Increase flicker to ±15% intensity at an irregular 2–4 Hz. Raise the point light intensity to 6 with distance 30, so a faint amber tint falls on the ash nearby.

Add about 200 instanced tiny ash flecks (0.03 m, #dfe6ff, emissive 0.8) drifting slowly upward within 15 m of the Wanderer. Add a low mist plane at y=0.15 in #3a4160 at 0.12 opacity, stretching toward the horizon. Add a faint star field of about 300 points in #cfd8ff with varied sizes on the sky dome.

But the posts are flat black cutouts with no rim light, so they read as pasted-on sticks, and the Wanderer's dark legs merge with them. The plain is a featureless blue sheet with a hard horizon line, and the overview shows the radial glow as a visible square patch. I'm steering toward silhouettes lit by a faint amber edge and a softer, hazier horizon.

critique: The well scene finally has a lovely focal cluster: the lantern's amber pool, the glowing hook and the faceted well all sit together against the cool plain. But the lantern's flat yellow disc sprite reads as a pasted-on plate in front of the well, and the black hook looks like a thin stick. The well is also lost in the bloom, with the black opening and petal barely visible. The overview shows two visible square patches on the ground, so the ground still needs softening. I'm steering toward a readable well with a bright petal, a rounder lantern glow, and seamless ground.

suggestions.change: Fix the flat disc look: make the core a small sphere (0.18 m, emissive intensity 2.5, #ffd27a) with a soft round halo, and make the halo mesh transparent with depthWrite false so it can't form a hard-edged plate. Reduce the sprite glow to 2.5 m at opacity 0.3. Set the point light to intensity 5, distance 24.

Make the petal readable on the rim: scale it to 0.14 m long, color #ffffff, emissive intensity 1.4, and raise its sprite glow to 0.8 m at opacity 0.5. Add 6 tiny pale motes (0.02 m) rising slowly from the well opening up to 1.5 m, and nudge it 0.05 m toward the wanderer so it sits clear of the rim.

Remove the visible square patches in the overview. Use CircleGeometry for every glow instead of PlaneGeometry, or fade the texture to exactly 0 at u/v borders (multiply by smoothstep(0.5,0.35,max(|u-0.5|,|v-0.5|))). Give the ground a faint gradient from #a9b1c4 near the well to #6c7690 beyond 60 m.

Lift the well from the bloom: raise block emissive to #3a4263 at 0.35 and add a thin cool rim light #8a90a3 on the north faces. Add a pale ash mound ring 2.2 m wide and 4 or 5 fallen stones (0.15 to 0.3 m, #4a5068) around the base so it sits in the ground.

The ground is still a flat blue sheet with hard dark shards at the horizon, and the arch's frost and cracks are lost at this distance. Add about 20 sparse frost motes (0.03 m, #e8f4ff) drifting upward within 2 m of the arch. Add about 120 more low ash mounds (#7d869b/#8f98ad, 0.8–2 m) in the near foreground around the Wanderer to break up the flat blue sheet.

critique: The frozen sea is a striking change: pale hexagonal plates on deep blue, a crowded sky, and a small glowing door-frame on the horizon. The plates are large, flat and evenly lit, so the ice reads as paper cutouts rather than glassy ice. The door's halo is nice, but the door is tiny and the sky's glow behind it is a flat wash. The arch's dark opening shows plates through it, which breaks the night-void look. I'm steering toward reflective depth in the ice, a stronger path to the door, and a crisper hero door.

suggestions.change: Add depth to the ice. Vary plate emissive and color by distance: near plates #6f7fa8 at 0.15 emissive, far plates #a9b1c4 at 0.35, so they brighten toward the door. Add thin dark crack lines (0.03 m wide, #0b1226) between plates using about 150 instanced thin boxes, 2–6 m long. Raise base ice emissive to #2a3d6a at 0.55 and shrink the nearest plates 30% so the foreground isn't big cutouts.

Make it the hero. Scale the frame to 0.14 m bars, raise the sprite halo to 8 m wide x 9 m tall at opacity 0.6, and add a vertical reflection streak on the ice: a feathered additive plane 1.5 m wide x 12 m long toward the Wanderer, #bfe4ff, opacity 0.18. Add a slow 0.1 opacity pulse.

Make the arch opening read as a true void: raise the dark plane opacity to 0.97 and set depthWrite true, so the ice plates don't show through. Keep the frost flecks and green-white tint on the pillars.

Add about 60 tiny pale-blue ice shards (0.1–0.3 m, #dfe6ff, emissive 0.5, instanced low octahedra) scattered along the line from the arch to the door, plus a low cold mist plane (#4a5580, opacity 0.1) 0.3 m over the ice. Add 15 faint star-reflection glints (#e8f4ff, 0.05 m) drifting upward slowly.

facts.description: The tall door of white light, about 3 m tall, now stands closer, its halo brighter and its starry interior showing a faint dark staircase going down.
facts.placement: about 10 m south of the wanderer on black_ice_sea

notes: Sank a row of six dark iron lanterns beneath the ice, shown as dim shapes under the glass, and etched a frosty heel crack behind you. The far door now glows brighter, with a dark staircase descending inside it.

ops.name: drowned_lanterns
ops.doc: Row of dark iron lanterns frozen under ice along +Z, seen as dim shapes; params: count, spacing, size

ops.name: ice_crack
ops.doc: Thin pale branching crack along -Z from local origin with frost crystals; params: length

ops.name: glow_door
ops.doc: Hero door of white light: bars, big halo, starry interior with dark descending staircase, ground glow, streak toward -Z; params: height, width, color

critique: The door glowing over the ice is a lovely cold beacon, and the halo, frost crystals and falling flakes give the foreground a hushed, snowy feel. But the drowned lanterns are invisible, so this turn's story beat is lost. The near plates are still flat, evenly lit slabs with hard dark edges, and the horizon is a hard dark band under a flat sky wash. I'm steering toward glassy depth under the ice, a readable lantern path leading to the door, and a softer, luminous horizon.

suggestions.change: Make them readable from behind the Wanderer. Raise the additive halo opacity from 0.12 to 0.3 in #8fa8d8 and scale it 2.2x. Add a faint dark-blue column under each, #0b1226 at opacity 0.4. Bring lantern depth to -0.7 m. Keep the iron bodies #23252f with a #8fc0ff rim at emissive 0.9. Do NOT light the flames. Space them evenly toward the door, passing just west of the Wanderer.

Give the ice glass depth. Cut the near plate scale another 25% and lower their emissive to 0.1. Add a feathered, slightly lighter #2a3d6a gradient to the base sheet toward the door. Add 40 thin pale translucent crack lines (#8fa8d8, opacity 0.35, 0.02 m wide, 1–3 m long) just under the surface. Soften the dark plate edges so they are not hard black cutouts.

Set skyBottom #5f6a9c and fogColor #55608f, and keep fogDensity at 0.014 so the sea dissolves into haze. Add a haze_band at the door's horizon (z about 80 from the door, #8fd0ff, 30 m wide, 6 m tall, opacity 0.12) so the sky behind the door has a soft gradient instead of a flat wash.

Scatter about 40 small pale frost crystals (0.05–0.15 m, #dfe6ff, emissive 0.5) along heel_crack and the boot path. Add a thin faint reflection of the door's glow on the ice: a feathered #bfe4ff additive plane 2 m wide and 14 m long, opacity 0.15, under the lantern line.

styleGuide: Palette: night indigo sky #070914 to #5f6a9c; ash silver-blue #8f98ad, #a9b1c4, #dfe6ff; stone greys #4a5068, #6f768a; bone-white #c9cfdc for the arch; black ice #1c2542 with pale plates #6f7fa8 to #a9b1c4, crack lines #0b1226 and under-ice glints #8fa8d8; dark wood/iron/robes #08090d, #23252f with cool rim #3a3f5c to #8fc0ff; warm amber #ffb347 only for lantern, fire and the Wanderer; pale blue #8fd0ff for shimmer, pool, thread; door white #eaf4ff; cold green-white #bfffe8 only for the south beacon and arch. Lighting: cool moonlit ambient, glowing ground, one warm point light. Fog dissolves edges into luminous haze. Materials: matte, powdery, glassy ice with soft emissive. Shapes: low-poly, faceted, sparse hero objects, large empty space. Glows round, feathered. Mood: quiet, lonely, uncanny cool promise.
